57-00-00-910-801Wing Skins - Corrosion PreventionPDF p. 41

2. Wing Skins - Corrosion Prevention

A. General

(1) Make the regular inspection to prevent or find the start of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery, or other corrosion deposits are signs of corrosion. Initiate the corrosion prevention practices to decrease the occurrence of corrosion. (2) Following cleaning of suspected areas PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701, a full inspection is effective to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads or joint edges), refer to Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to decrease the corrosion process. Refer to PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701 for details on applying corrosion inhibiting compound. The finish system should be repaired at the next maintenance opportunity.

B. References

Reference Title 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification A50193 Sealant - Pressure And Environmental-Chromate (For Spray Application As A Primer) BMS5-95 Type I Class F C00175 Primer - Urethane Compatible, Corrosion Resistant BMS10-79 Type III C50262 Coating - Protective Enamel (BAC 900 Clear Color) BMS10-60 Type II G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 500 Left Wing 600 Right Wing 57-00-00

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-00-00-370-001 (1) At first opportunity consistent with the scheduled maintenance activity, apply corrosion prevention treatment to the wing in-spar skin. (a) Apply the primer, C00175 and the coating, C50262 for the wing in-spar upper skin and apply the sealant, A50193 and coating, C50262 for the wing in-spar lower skin. SUBTASK 57-00-00-370-002 (2) Frequency of Application (a) Periodic inspection is required in areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules specified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrences. (b) Periodic application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 is necessary to areas identified and should be consistent to the schedule specified in the Maintenance Planning Document.

57-14-00-910-801Wing Center Section - Corrosion PreventionPDF p. 515

2. Wing Center Section - Corrosion Prevention

A. General

(1) Make a regular inspection to prevent or find the start of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery, or other corrosion deposits are signs of corrosion. Initiate the corrosion prevention practices to decrease the occurrence of corrosion. (2) Following cleaning of suspected areas (PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701), a full inspection is effective to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads or joint edges), refer to the Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to decrease the corrosion process. Refer to PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701 for details on applying corrosion inhibiting compound. The finish system should be repaired at the next maintenance opportunity.

B. References

Reference Title 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification C00033 Coating - Protective Enamel, Flexibility Use BMS10-60 Type II C00175 Primer - Urethane Compatible, Corrosion Resistant BMS10-79 Type III C00259 Coating - Chemical And Solvent Resistant Finish, Corrosion Inhibiting Primer BMS10-11 Type I G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 135 Area Above Wing Center Section, Body Station 540 to Body Station 663.75 - Left 57-14-00 (Continued) Zone Area 136 Area Above Wing Center Section, Body Station 540 to Body Station 663.75 - Right

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-14-00-100-001 (1) Clean the affected area to remove corrosion products . SUBTASK 57-14-00-370-005 (2) Apply 2 coats of primer, C00175 or primer, C00259 to areas where the paint is missing. SUBTASK 57-14-00-390-001 (3) If you used primer, C00175, coating, C00033 may be applied to the area for additional corrosion protection. Do not apply coating, C00033 if you used primer, C00259. SUBTASK 57-14-00-370-004 (4) Frequency of Application (a) Periodic inspection is required in areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules specified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrences. (b) Periodic application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 is necessary to areas identified and should be consistent to the schedule specified in the Maintenance Planning Document.

57-15-00-910-801Main Landing Gear Support Beam - Corrosion PreventionPDF p. 519

2. Main Landing Gear Support Beam - Corrosion Prevention

A. General

(1) Make the regular inspection to prevent or find the start of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery, or other corrosion deposits are signs of corrosion. Initiate the corrosion prevention practices to decrease the occurrence of corrosion. (2) Following cleaning of suspected areas PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701, a full inspection is effective to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads or joint edges), refer to Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to decrease the corrosion process. Refer to PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701 for details on applying corrosion inhibiting compound. The finish system should be repaired at the next maintenance opportunity.

B. References

Reference Title 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING 57-15-00

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-001 (1) At first opportunity consistent with the scheduled maintenance activity, apply corrosion prevention treatment to the main landing gear trunnion support structure. SUBTASK 57-15-00-200-002 (2) Periodically inspect the main landing gear beam and the forward trunnion fitting attached to the rear spar for damaged finish and evidence of corrosion. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-002 (3) Apply water displacing corrosion inhibiting compound to landing gear beams. SUBTASK 57-15-00-910-001 (4) Remove runway debris and clean the entire wheel well area. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-003 (5) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to all exposed wheel well structure. Pay particular attention to applying the corrosion inhibitor along doubler edges, along edges of structure, forgings, etc., and on fastener heads. Use spray equipment with nozzle directed into faying surfaces. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-004 (6) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to landing gear attachment fittings. Make sure to apply the compound to lugs and lug faces. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-005 (7) Regrease all grease fittings in the treatment area. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-006 (8) After cleaning the wheel well with steam or high pressure water and detergent, apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009. SUBTASK 57-15-00-200-003 (9) Periodically inspect heavily loaded structural members and wheel well closure walls for deterioration of protective finishes. SUBTASK 57-15-00-370-007 (10) Frequency of Application (a) Periodic inspection is required in areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules specified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrences. (b) Periodic application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 is necessary to areas identified and should be consistent to the schedule specified in the Maintenance Planning Document.

D. Prepare to Remove the Support Beam

SUBTASK 57-15-00-860-001 (1) To defuel the wing fuel tanks, do this task: Fuel T ank Defueling, TASK 28-26-00-650-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-860-002 (2) To remove the applicable inboard trailing edge flap, do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Transmission Removal, TASK 27-51-31-000-802. SUBTASK 57-15-00-860-003 (3) Lower the trailing edge flaps. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-002 (4) To remove the applicable main landing gear, do this task: Main Landing Gear Removal, TASK 32-11-00-000-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-010-001 (5) To remove the wing door, do this task: Main Landing Gear Wing Door Removal, TASK 32-13-21-000-802. SUBTASK 57-15-00-010-002 (6) To remove the fairing for the inboard flap track, do this task: Inboard Flap Support Aft Fairing Removal, TASK 27-51-18-000-802. 57-15-00 SUBTASK 57-15-00-010-003 (7) To remove the applicable inboard ground spoiler, do this task: Inboard Ground Spoiler Removal, TASK 27-62-12-000-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-200-001 (8) At the fitting on the rear spar holding the outboard end of the support beam, measure to find if it is necessary to install new bushings. NOTE: The installation of new bushings will be done after removing the support beam completely. (a) Measure the clearance between the bushing face on the FORWARD side of the support beam and adjacent bushing face in the support fitting. 1) This clearance cannot be more than 0.020 in. (0.508 mm). (b) Measure the clearance between the bushing face on the AFT side of the support beam and the adjacent bushing face in the support fitting. 1) This clearance cannot be more than 0.020 in. (0.508 mm). 2) The total clearance, aft side plus the forward side, cannot be more than 0.025 in. (0.635 mm). (c) If these clearances are more than the allowed limits, replace defective bushings. NOTE: Shim washers are not allowed. NOTE: Defective bushings may be in the support beam and/or the support fitting. SUBTASK 57-15-00-010-004 (9) Remove the applicable panels surrounding the main landing gear support beam: (a) On the left wing, remove these access panels: Number Name/Location 551AT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge Access Panel 551BT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Actuator Access Panel 551DT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Beam Access Panel 551ET Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Structural MLG Beam Access Panel (b) On the left wing, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 551DB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Lube Actuator & MLG Beam Outboard Attach Pin Access Panel (c) On the left wing, remove these access panels: (TASK 57-50-02-000-801) Number Name/Location 551EB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Attach Fitting Access Panel 551FB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Landing Gear Access Panel (d) On the right wing, remove these access panels: Number Name/Location 651AT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge Access Panel 651BT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Actuator Access Panel 651DT Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Beam Access Panel 57-15-00 (Continued) Number Name/Location 651ET Upper Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Beam Access Panel (e) On the right wing, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 651DB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Lube Actuator & MLG Beam Outboard Attach Pin Access Panel (f) On the right wing, remove these access panels: (TASK 57-50-02-000-801) Number Name/Location 651EB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, MLG Attach Fitting Access Panel 651FB Lower Inboard Fixed Trailing Edge, Landing Gear Access Panel

E. Landing Gear Support Beam Removal

SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-003 (1) Remove the upper and lower stabilizer links (Figure 401). (a) Remove the cotter pin [8], nut [7], fuse pin [4], washer [5], and washer [6] which connect the forward end of the lower stabilizer link [3] to the attach fitting on the rear spar. (b) Disconnect the bonding jumper. (c) Remove the cotter pin [8], nut [7], fuse pin [4], washer [5], and washer [6] which connect the aft end of the lower stabilizer link [3] to the attach fitting on the support beam. (d) Disconnect the jumper. (e) Remove the four bolts [9] and four collars [10] which connect the two tray brackets to the upper stabilizer link [14]. (f) Remove the cotter pin [13], nut [12], bolt [15], washer [16], and washer [11] which connect the aft end of the upper stabilizer link [14] to the attach fitting on the support beam. (g) Remove the cotter pin [8], nut [7], fuse pin [4], washer [5], and washer [6] which connect the forward end of the upper stabilizer link [14] to the attach fitting on the rear spar. (h) Disconnect the bonding jumper. (i) If it is necessary, remove the bolts from the upper and lower stabilizer link attach fittings on the support beam,. 1) Remove the attach fittings from the support beam. 2) Make a note of the location of the shims. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-004 (2) To remove the walking beam hanger fitting, the walking beam, and the actuator, do this task: Removal of the Actuator Assembly for the Main Gear, TASK 32-32-11-000-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-005 (3) To remove the two ground spoiler actuators from the aft side of the support beam, do this task: Inboard Ground Spoiler Actuator Removal, TASK 27-62-71-000-801. (a) Also, remove the two spoiler hinge supports, if necessary. 57-15-00 SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-006 (4) Disconnect the necessary hydraulic and fire extinguishing tubes from the support beam. NOTE: These tubes are on the aft and the forward side of the support beam. (a) Make a note of the locations of the tubes. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-007 (5) Disconnect the necessary electrical wires from the support beam. (a) Make sure that there is no tension in the wires. NOTE: The wires must be loose for removal of the support beam. SUBTASK 57-15-00-970-001 (6) Make a note of the location of the wires. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-008 (7) To remove the inboard flap inboard transmission, do this task: Inboard Flap Inboard Transmission Removal, TASK 27-51-31-000-802. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-009 (8) To remove the inboard flap outboard transmission if necessary, do this task: Inboard Flap Outboard Transmission Removal, TASK 27-51-31-000-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-010 (9) To remove the main landing gear beam angle gear box from the aft side of the support beam, do this task: Main Landing Gear Beam Angle Gearbox Removal, TASK 27-51-56-000-801. WITHOUT CORRECT TOOLS TO SUPPORT THIS WEIGHT , INJURY TO PERSONS AND/OR DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 7) If you will remove the hanger link [39] from the airplane, do these steps: a) Remove the pin [43], bolt [40], countersunk washer [41], caps [42], washer [46], self-locking nut [44], nut [45], collar [49], radius filler [48], bolt [47], self-locking nut [50], bolt [54], countersunk washer [53], washer [51], and bushing [52]. b) Remove the hanger link [39]. (c) Remove the nut [30], washer [31], washer [32], and bolt [33] (4 locations) from the attach fitting at the inboard end of the support beam. NOTE: This attach fitting connects the support beam to the inboard flap track. See illustration. (d) Remove the outboard attach the fuse pin [34], two bolts [35], two washers [36], two bushings [37], and two nuts [38]. (e) Carefully remove the support beam. 1) Move the support beam inboard until it is clear of the fitting at the outboard end, electrical wire bundles, fire extinguishing tube, and hydraulic tubes. 2) Lower the outboard end of the beam and move the beam outboard. 3) Remove the support beam from the airplane.

(1) Install the outboard end of the main landing gear support beam [1] or main landing gear support beam [2]. (a) Put the support beam into its position. 1) Lift the inboard end of the support beam and move it inboard until it is above any structure. 2) Lift the outboard end of the support beam. 3) Put the outboard end of the support beam in the outboard support fitting. 4) Hold the support beam in its position. (b) Attach the support beam to the rear spar support fitting. 1) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the outer diameter and threads of the outboard attach fuse pin [34]. 2) Install the outboard attach fuse pin [34], two bolts [35], two washers [36], two bushings [37], and two nuts [38] to connect the rear spar support fitting and the outboard end of the support beam. a) Tighten the nuts [38] on the bolts [35] to 250 in-lb (28.2 N·m) - 300 in-lb (33.9 N·m). SUBTASK 57-15-00-420-003 (2) Reconnect the inboard end of the main landing gear support beam [1] or main landing gear support beam [2] to the airplane as follows: (a) Install the attach fitting at the inboard end of the support beam. 1) Put the attach fitting into its place. 2) Install the nut [30], nut [30A], washer [31], washer [31A], washer [32], washer [32A], bolt [33], and bolt [33A]. (b) If you removed the hanger link [39] from the airplane, do these steps: 1) Put the hanger link [39] into its position. a) Before installation the pin [43], apply a light coat of grease, D00633, to its outer diameter and threads. b) Install the pin [43], bolt [40], countersunk washer [41], caps [42], washer [46], self-locking nut [44], nut [45], collars [49], radius fillers [48], and bolt [47]. c) Tighten the nut [45] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m) - 2000 in-lb (226.0 N·m). d) Tighten the self-locking nut [44] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m) - 1200 in-lb (135.6 N·m). 2) Install the bolt [54], self-locking nut [50], countersunk washer [53], washer [51], and bushing [52]. a) Before you install the bushing, apply a light coat of grease, grease, D00633, to its outer diameter. b) Tighten the self-locking nut [50] to 480 in-lb (54.2 N·m) - 790 in-lb (89.3 N·m). 57-15-00 (c) To connect the lower end of the hanger link [39] to the support beam, do these steps: 1) Install the pin [20], two nuts [23], two collars [24], two radius fillers [25], two bolts [26], washer [27], washer [28], and washer [29] on the hanger link [39], (Figure 401). NOTE: Install the washer [27], washer [28], and washer [29], with the quantity as required, between the bushing flanges at each side of the support beam to reduce the gap to a minimum of 0.005 in. (0.127 mm) per side and 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) maximum total for both sides. a) Apply a light coat of grease, D00633 on the outer diameter and threads of the pin [20]. b) Tighten the nut [23] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m) - 2000 in-lb (226.0 N·m). 2) Install the bolt [17], washer [18], two caps [19], washer [21], and self-locking nut [22]. 3) Tighten the self-locking nut [22] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m) - 1200 in-lb (135.6 N·m). (3.302 mm) between the wire bundles and hangar link. (e) Apply grease, D00633, through all grease fittings on the hanger link until grease can be seen coming out. D. Hanger Link Pins and Bushings Inspection

NOTE: This is an alternate procedure for the inspection of hanger link pins and bushings, without the removal of the landing gear support beam. For the inspection of all bolts, pins and bushings which attach the support beam, refer to Inspection Procedure for Support Beam Bolts, Pins and Bushings. SUBTASK 57-15-00-020-014 (1) To remove the lower pin from the hanger link and support beam, do this task: Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin Removal, TASK 57-15-01-020-801. SUBTASK 57-15-00-210-002 (2) Look for worn areas on the lower pin and bushings of the hanger link, (Figure 601, View A-A). (a) Use a micrometer (0-1 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1096, or a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097, to measure the diameters of the pins and the bushings. (b) Compare the measured dimensions with the permitted dimensions shown in (Figure 601). (c) Replace the parts which are out of the tolerance. NOTE: If a part is replaced on the hanger link, replace the corresponding part to keep symmetry. 57-15-00 SUBTASK 57-15-00-420-013 (3) To install the lower pin to the hanger link and support beam, do this task: Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin Installation, TASK 57-15-01-420-801.

(1.270 mm), do as follows: 1) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin Removal, TASK 57-15-01-020-801. 2) Measure the maximum inner diameter and minimum wall thickness of the hangar link and landing gear bushings. 3) Do a detailed visual inspection of the pin and bushings for wear (TASK 57-15-00-200-801). NOTE: If damage other than worn bushings is found, contact for more repair instructions. a) If it is damaged, replace the bushings. NOTE: If a bushing is replaced on a part of the hangar link or the landing beam, replace all worn bushings common to that part. b) If it is damaged, replace the pin. NOTE: A small discoloration because of the material transfer from the bushing to the pin is permitted. 4) Make sure that the joint area is clean and free of unwanted material. a) Remove all the remaining grease, unwanted material, and other contamination. 5) Add grease to the joint. 6) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin Installation, TASK 57-15-01-420-801. Reference Title 07-11-01 P/B 201 JACK AIRPLANE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201) 57-15-00 P/B 401 MAIN LANDING GEAR SUPPORT BEAM - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION 57-15-00 P/B 601 LANDING GEAR SUPPORT BEAM - INSPECTION/CHECK

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

C. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 57-15-01-480-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801. SUBTASK 57-15-01-580-001 (2) Do this task: JACK AIRPLANE - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES, PAGEBLOCK 07-11-01/201. NOTE: Do not rest the MLG beam directly against a metal jack pad. Use a wooden block or similar to protect the MLG beam from damage. Support the MLG beam with a jack so that the load against the hanger link can be adjusted to facilitate removal of the hanger link bolts. NOTE: Do not allow the jack to depressurize or adjust the jacks supporting the airplane while the hanger link pins are removed as this could cause unacceptable preload against interfacing structural and system elements. SUBTASK 57-15-01-010-001 (3) Get access to the main landing gear support beam lower flange. 57-15-01

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-15-01-020-001 (1) Disconnect the lower and upper pins from the support beam, do these steps: WARNING MAKE CERTAIN LANDING GEAR DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED TO PREVENT INADVERTENT RETRACTION OF LANDING GEAR, AND POSSIBLE INJURY TO PERSONNEL. (a) Remove the nut [10], washer [11], bolt [1], countersunk washer [2], caps [3], collars [13], bolts [8], radius fillers [9], nut [12], lower pin [4], washers [7], washers [6] and washers [5] from the hanger link. NOTE: Make a note of the location of all the washers. (b) Keep all of the washers. (c) Remove the nut [20], washer [21], bolt [29], countersunk washer [28], caps [27], collars [24], bolts [22], radius fillers [23], nut [25] and upper pin [30]. (d) Do a detailed visual inspection of the bushings [14] for wear, refer to AMM TASK LANDING GEAR SUPPORT BEAM - INSPECTION/CHECK, PAGEBLOCK 57-15-00/601. 1) If necessary, remove the hanger link [26] for repair or replacement, refer to AMM TASK MAIN LANDING GEAR SUPPORT BEAM - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 57-15-00/401. 2) If damaged, replace the bushings [14], refer to AMM TASK MAIN LANDING GEAR SUPPORT BEAM - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 57-15-00/401. NOTE: If a bushing is replaced on a part of the hanger link, replace all worn bushings common to that part.

57-15-01-420-801Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin InstallationPDF p. 565

3. Main Landing Gear Support Beam Hanger Links Upper And Lower Pin Installation (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 07-11-01-580-816 Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks (P/B 201)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1022 Wrench - Torque, 1000 to 2000 in-lbs (112.98 to 225.96 N-m), +/-5% accuracy

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification D00633 Grease - Aircraft General Purpose BMS3-33

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 734 Left Main Landing Gear 744 Right Main Landing Gear

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-15-01-420-001 (1) Install the upper pin [30] to the hanger link [26]. (a) Before you install the upper pin [30], apply a thin layer of grease, D00633 to its outer diameter and threads. (b) Install the upper pin [30] and nut [25]. (c) Tighten the nut [25] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m)-2000 in-lb (226.0 N·m) with a torque wrench, STD-1022. (d) Install the radius fillers [23], bolts [22] and collars [24]. (e) Install the bolt [29], countersunk washer [28], caps [27], washer [21] and nut [20]. (f) Tighten the nut [20] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m)-1200 in-lb (135.6 N·m) with a torque wrench, STD-1022. SUBTASK 57-15-01-420-003 (2) To connect the lower end of the hanger link [26] to the support beam, do these steps: (a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633 on the outer diameter and threads of the lower pin [4]. (b) Install the washers [5], washers [6], washers [7], lower pin [4] and nut [12] on the hanger link [26]. NOTE: Install the washers [5], washers [6], and washers [7] between the bushing flanges at each side of the support beam to reduce the gap to a minimum of 0.005 in. (0.127 mm) per side and 0.025 in. (0.635 mm) maximum total for both sides. (c) Tighten the nut [12] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m)-2000 in-lb (226.0 N·m) with a torque wrench, STD-1022. (d) Install the radius fillers [9], bolts [8] and collars [13]. (e) Install the bolt [1], countersunk washer [2], caps [3], washer [11] and nut [10]. 57-15-01 (f) Tighten the nut [10] to 1000 in-lb (113.0 N·m)-1200 in-lb (135.6 N·m) with a torque wrench, STD-1022. (g) Apply grease, D00633 through all the grease fittings on the hanger link [26] until the grease comes out. F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 57-15-01-580-002 (1) Do this task: Lower the Airplane Off the Jacks, TASK 07-11-01-580-816.

E. MLG Aft Trunnion Bearing Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 57-16-02-420-001 (1) Install the lock plate [8]. (a) Install the bushings [11] in the Main Landing Gear (MLG) support beam (TASK 20-10-02-900-801). 1) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the outer diameter of the bushings [11]. 2) Shrink fit the bushings [11] in their positions. (b) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the outer diameter of the bushings [10]. (c) Install the bushings [10] in the lock plate [8]. (d) Put the lock plate [8] in its position. (e) Install the bolts [9], washers [12], and nuts [13]. 1) Tighten the nuts [13] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m) - 30 in-lb (3.4 N·m). 57-16-02 SUBTASK 57-16-02-020-004 (2) Install the split ball assembly [7] and outer race assembly [5]. NOTE: Installation of the race assembly grease fitting should be on the upper inboard side of the trunnion pin when looking forward, approximately 2 o'clock orientation for the left hand side and 11 o'clock orientation for the right hand side. (a) Apply a thin coat of grease, D00633, or grease, D00013, to all parts before you install them. NOTE: grease, D00633, is the preferred grease because it offers protection against corrosion and oxidation. (b) Make sure that the wider splines of the outer race assembly [5] and lock plate are aligned (View C, Figure 401). SUBTASK 57-16-02-020-005 (3) Install the retainer nut [1]. (a) Tighten the retainer nut [1] to 10 ft-lb (13.6 N·m) - 15 ft-lb (20.3 N·m). 1) Use the wrench adaptor, SPL-11076, to tighten the retainer nut [1]. 2) After the initial torque, allow excess grease on the outer race assembly [5] and split ball assembly [7] to extrude from the bearing housing. a) Recheck the torque to ensure it is still within the torque limits. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE END OF THE OUTER RACE ASSEMBLY IS FLUSH WITH THE TOP OF THE RETAINER NUT WHILE YOU TIGHTEN THE RETAINER NUT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE INCORRECT POSITION OF THE GREASE FITTING TO THE LANDING GEAR. (b) Make sure that the end of the outer race assembly [5] is flush with the top of the retainer nut [1] while you tighten the retainer nut [1] (View C, Figure 401). SUBTASK 57-16-02-020-006 (4) Install the lock tab [4] to the lock plate. (a) Back the retainer nut [1] off until tab can engage slot in nut. 1) To do this, these steps can help: a) The lock tab [4] can be flipped. b) The lock tab [4] can be moved to adjacent threaded holes in the lock plate. (b) Install the screws [2], washers [3], and lockwire. 1) Tighten the screws [2] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.0 N·m). 2) Install the lockwire by the double-twist procedure. SUBTASK 57-16-02-020-007 (5) Lubricate the aft trunnion bearing assembly at the lubrication fitting using grease, D00633. (a) Move the spherical bearing until positioned as shown in View A-A, Figure 401. NOTE: Grease shall appear at inner diameter of bearing. SUBTASK 57-16-02-020-008 (6) Install the aft trunnion pin [6] into the aft trunnion bearing assembly. 57-16-02 F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 57-16-02-010-003 (1) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Installation, TASK 32-11-00-400-801. SUBTASK 57-16-02-010-006 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).

MLG Rear Spar Stablizer Attachment Fitting Assembly Removal SUBTASK 57-16-03-040-001 (1) Make sure that the pressure from all the hydraulics has been removed (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). (d) Make sure that the gap between the aft face of the fitting and the rear spar is not greater than 0.0050 in. (0.1270 mm) before clamp up. 1) If a gap greater than 0.0050 in. (0.1270 mm) is found, disassemble the assembly and look for unwanted material between the mated parts. G. MLG Support Beam Outboard Fitting Assembly Removal

SUBTASK 57-16-04-040-001 (1) Make sure that the pressure from the hydraulic systems have been removed (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or TASK 29-09-00-860-808). SUBTASK 57-16-04-020-006 (2) Disconnect the necessary hydraulic tubes and fire extinguisher lines around the fitting assembly (TASK 20-10-51-000-801). (a) Install protective caps on the ends of the hydraulic tubes. (b) Make a note of the location of the lines. 57-16-04 (c) If it is necessary, clean up the hydraulic fluid (TASK 12-40-00-100-801 or TASK 12-40-00-100-803). SUBTASK 57-16-04-020-007 (3) Disconnect the necessary electrical wires around the assembly. (a) Make note of the location of the wires. SUBTASK 57-16-04-000-002 (4) Remove the MLG Support Beam Outboard Fitting Assembly. (a) On the outboard side of the MLG Support Beam Outboard Fitting Assembly, remove the following: 1) Remove the six bolts [5], six washers [8], and six nuts [9] which connect the upper part of the support fitting [1] assembly to the upper part of the rear spar. 2) Remove the six bolts [7], six washers [11], and six nuts [10] which connect the lower part of the support fitting [1] assembly to the lower part of the rear spar. 3) Remove the four bolts [13] and four nuts [6] which connect the aft of the support fitting [1] assembly to the rear spar. 4) Remove the 10 bolts [14] and 10 collars [4] which connect the aft of the support fitting [1] assembly to the rear spar. (b) On the inboard side of the MLG Support Beam Outboard Fitting Assembly, remove the following: 1) Remove the six bolts [17], six washers [27], and six nuts [26] which connect the upper part of the support fitting [1] assembly the upper part of the rear spar. 2) Remove the six bolts [20], six washers [24], and six nuts [25] which connect the lower part of the support fitting [1] assembly to the lower part of the rear spar. 3) Remove the four bolts [22] and four nuts [19] which connect the aft of the support fitting [1] assembly to the rear spar. 4) Remove the remaining bolts [23] and collars [18] which connect the aft of the support fitting [1] assembly to the rear spar. NOTE: For the left wing fitting assembly, there are ten locations. For the right wing fitting assembly, there are twelve locations. (c) Remove the support fitting [1] assembly and the shims from the rear spar. 1) Remove the shims from the support fitting assembly. a) Make note of the location of the shims. 2) Carefully remove the fitting assembly from airplane. SUBTASK 57-16-04-800-001 (5) For more information on the support fitting assembly refer to: (a) CMM 57–15–01: Main Landing Gear Beam Installation Components.

57-20-00-910-801Outer Wing - Corrosion PreventionPDF p. 623

2. Outer Wing - Corrosion Prevention

A. General

(1) Make the regular inspection to prevent or find the start of corrosion. Missing fasteners, white powdery, or other corrosion deposits are signs of corrosion. Initiate the corrosion prevention practices to decrease the occurrence of corrosion. 57-20-00 (2) Following cleaning of suspected areas PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701, a full inspection is effective to ensure that protective finishes provided during manufacture remain intact. (3) Where corrosion exists (noticeable bulges of the skin or white deposits of corrosion products at fastener heads or joint edges), refer to Structural Repair Manual for details of corrosion removal. (4) For minor corrosion, to minimize the downtime of the airplane, the corrosion products should be cleaned off, followed by the application of a corrosion inhibiting compound into the affected area to decrease the corrosion process. Refer to PAGEBLOCK 51-21-91/701 for details on applying corrosion inhibiting compound. The finish system should be repaired at the next maintenance opportunity.

B. References

Reference Title 12-20-00-640-801 General Instructions for Lubrication (P/B 301) 51-21-31 P/B 701 CORROSION REMOVAL AND CONTROL - CLEANING/PAINTING 51-21-91 P/B 701 CORROSION INHIBITING COMPOUND - CLEANING/PAINTING

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification D50050 Grease - Multipurpose, Helicopter Oscillating Bearing Grease with Calcium Soap Thickener - Aeroshell 14 MIL-G-25537 G00009 Compound - Organic Corrosion Inhibiting BMS3-23 G50237 Compound - Corrosion Inhibiting, Non-drying - Cor-Ban 27L BMS3-38

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 500 Left Wing 600 Right Wing

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-20-00-370-001 (1) At first opportunity consistent with scheduled maintenance activity, apply corrosion prevention treatment to the front and rear spars, wing internal structure, and the fuel tank and boost pump access cutout. SUBTASK 57-20-00-200-001 (2) Replace damaged or broken finishes. NOTE: When refinishing the areas around fasteners, inspect around fasteners to ensure that corrosion is not present and apply fillet seal around fasteners prior to paint finishing. SUBTASK 57-20-00-910-001 (3) Do these steps to prevent corrosion on front spar and rear spar: (a) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the forward surface areas of the front spar. Pay particular attention to spar chord and web joints and faying surfaces of stiffeners, brackets, etc. Use the spray equipment with nozzle directed into faying surfaces, General Instructions for Lubrication, TASK 12-20-00-640-801. 57-20-00 (b) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound to the aft surface areas of the rear spar. Pay particular attention to the spar chord and web joints, faying surfaces of stiffeners, brackets, etc., and around high strength boltheads, General Instructions for Lubrication, TASK 12-20-00-640-801. (c) Regrease all grease fittings in treatment area, General Instructions for Lubrication, TASK 12-20-00-640-801. NOTE: The expansion of the corroded material may cause a localized lifting of the free end of the chord flange. This lifting can be detected by checking the chord surface for flatness using a straightedge or scanning with fingers. In some cases, instead of chord flange lifting, the spar web may be depressed. Local depression of the web generally occurs where the spar chord flange is stiffer than the web. These web depressions can be detected visually. SUBTASK 57-20-00-910-002 (4) Do these steps to prevent corrosion in wing internal structure: (a) Corrosion prevention includes drainage of water, controlling microbial growth, and making periodic inspection. (b) Inspect the limber holes and drain tubes to make sure the drainage of water, when entering the wing (c) There are three options for the removal of water or prevention of corrosion: 1) Installing a water scavenge system. 2) Adding sealant to fill areas where water accumulates. 3) Using Strontium chromate canisters to inhibit corrosion (d) Refer to Structural Repair Manual for details on removing corrosion if extensive corrosion exists on the wing inspar skin. (5) Restore integral fuel tank finish. SUBTASK 57-20-00-910-003 (6) Do these steps to prevent corrosion in fuel tank and boost pump cutouts: (a) Inspect the mating surfaces of the access door clamp ring and wing skin at regularly scheduled maintenance periods to find corrosion. (b) If there is no corrosion, install the access clamp rings with knitted aluminum gaskets after applying anti-corrosion compound for corrosion protection. Apply 0.010 - 0.015 inches of Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 or Aeroshell 14 helicopter grease, D50050 to wing skin faying surface prior to installing door ring and gasket. NOTE: Aeroshell 14 helicopter grease, D50050 is the recommended anti-corrosion compound for access door gasket installations. Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, can still be used for access door gaskets, but should be replaced with Aeroshell 14 helicopter grease, D50050 as soon as practical. 1) Do not mix the two types of anti-corrosion compounds, Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 and Aeroshell 14 helicopter grease, D50050. When applying the recommended anti-corrosion compound, Aeroshell 14 helicopter grease, D50050, make sure to remove all Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 from the mesh gasket, clamp ring and the access door structure on the airplane. (c) If there is corrosion, refer to Structural Repair Manual for corrosion removal. SUBTASK 57-20-00-370-002 (7) Frequency of Application 57-20-00 (a) Periodic inspection is required in areas identified as susceptible to corrosion and should be consistent to the schedules specified in the Maintenance Planning Document. Operators must be aware of reported problems and areas of occurrences. (b) Periodic application of corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 is necessary to areas identified and should be consistent to the schedule specified in the Maintenance Planning Document.

NOTE: The sling equipment has three attachment fittings, six screws and washers, a sling strap assembly, a load cell, STD-12395. 57-21-21 097-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (Continued) (a) Remove the 6 bolts from the winglet [10] where the attachment fittings for the sling, SPL-2044, will be attached to the winglet [10]. 1) Store the bolts in a bag for the installation procedure. (b) Install 6 bolts and washers to attach the 3 attachment fittings to the winglet [10]. 1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) to 80 in-lb (9 N·m). NOTE: The attachment bolts and washers for the sling are stored in the threaded storage holes on the end surfaces of the attachment fittings. (c) Attach the sling strap assembly to the three fittings with the short strap attached to the upper, outboard fitting of the winglet [10]. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-002 (2) Attach the sling, SPL-2044, to the overhead crane (Figure 401). NOTE: The winglet weighs approximately 137 lb (62 kg). (3) Use the load cell, STD-12395, to make sure that the force used when lifting the winglet [10] is not more than 150 lb (68 kg). NOTE: The value for the weight of the winglet is 140 lb (64 kg). (a) Balance the overhead crane tension, so you can loosen the bolts that hold the winglet [10] to the wing, without damage to the bolt threads or to the winglet [10]. SUBTASK 57-21-21-490-004 (5) Use an explosion proof flashlight, STD-1081, when you look inside the dry bay tank. (c) Store the each set of bolts and washers in a separate bag for the installation procedure; label the bag as the diameters and lengths are different for each attachment location. (11.1125 mm) diameter. 2) Apply force with the torque wrench in a clockwise direction. 3) If the bolts can be torqued until the threads protrude, then the barrel nuts in the winglet [10] must be replaced. (e) Install the barrel nut [16] with retainer [15] through the access holes in the wing root of the winglet [10]. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-015 (6) Install the sling, SPL-2044, on the winglet (Figure 402). NOTE: The sling equipment has three attachment fittings, six screws and washers, a sling strap assembly, a load cell, STD-12395. (a) Remove the 6 bolts from the replacement winglet [10] where the attachment fittings for the sling, SPL-2044, will be attached to the winglet [10]. 1) Store the 6 screws in a bag. (b) Attach the 3 attachment fittings to the winglet [10] with 6 screws and washers. 1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) to 80 in-lb (9 N·m). (c) Attach the sling straps to the 3 attachment fittings with the short line attached to the upper leading edge of the winglet [10]. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-016 (7) Attach the sling, SPL-2044, to the overhead, 250 lb capacity lift crane, STD-247 (Figure 402). NOTE: The winglet weighs approximately 137 lb (62 kg). 57-21-21 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-096 (Continued) SUBTASK 57-21-21-800-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE FORCE WITHOUT THE TOOL WEIGHT IS NO MORE THAN THE SPECIFIED FORCE. A FORCE THAT IS MORE THAN THE SPECIFIED FORCE CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (8) Use the load cell, STD-12395, to make sure that the force used when lifting the winglet [10] is not more than 150 lb (68 kg). NOTE: The value for the weight of the winglet is 140 lb (64 kg). SUBTASK 57-21-21-500-004 (9) Operate the overhead crane to lift the sling until the 3 lines are equally supporting the winglet [10]. (a) Balance the overhead crane tension, so you can tighten the bolts that hold the winglet [10] to the wing, without damage to the bolt threads or to the winglet [10]. SUBTASK 57-21-21-410-004 (10) Connect the forward grounding strap [12] and aft grounding strap [11] (Figure 402). (a) You must control movement of the sling and the winglet [10] as you install the attachment fasteners for the grounding straps. NOTE: A second person is recommended to control the movement of the winglet which is suspended from the crane and sling. A gust of wind could cause the winglet to move as you install the attachment fasteners for the grounding straps. (b) Do not pull the winglet [10] away from the wing, the forward and aft grounding straps are attached between the winglet [10] and the wing outboard rib. (c) Install the lug of the grounding strap on the electrical stud on the wing rib. (d) Install a washer [8] and nut [9] and tighten. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-022 (11) Connect the anti-collision and position light connectors to the winglet [10] electrical receptacles [18] (View A-A, Figure 402): (a) Do this task: Anti-Collision Lights - Connect the Electrical Connector, TASK 33-44-13-420-801. (b) Do this task: Position Lights - Connect the Electrical Connector, TASK 33-43-10-420-801. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-018 (12) Install the winglet [10] (Figure 402). (a) Refer to the table: Table 404. (b) If you did not keep the bolts in separate bags or you replace the bolt, make sure the bolt grip length is correct for the installation location. (c) Apply a thin coat of corrosion inhibitiing compound - ZC-027L, A50001, or Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, to all surfaces of the bolt threads, shanks, and under the bolt head prior to installation. (d) Install the four bolts [1], two bolts [2] and two bolts [3] with the order sequence in the table. 1) Refer to the table: Table 404. 2) Do not tighten the bolts to the final torque value at this time. 57-21-21 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-096 (Continued) a) Install the bolt [1] and washer [5] one at a time in number order until seated in the correct hole. b) Install the two bolts [2] and washers [5] one at a time in number order until seated in the correct hole. c) Install the two bolts [3] and washers [5] one at a time in number order until seated in the correct hole. (e) Install the 10 bolts [4] and washers [6], one at a time, until seated; do not tighten the bolts to the final torque value at this time. SUBTASK 57-21-21-210-001 (1) Inspect the attachment holes on the upper and lower surfaces. Refer to SRM 51-10-02. SUBTASK 57-21-21-210-002 (2) Make sure that the holes are within the hole tolerances shown in Figure 403.

H. Blended Winglet Tip Fairing Installation

SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-025 (1) Put the fairing [25] in position and make sure all gaps and mismatches are within the tolerances shown in Figure 403. 57-21-21 SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-014 (2) If necessary, apply a protective coating to the bare surfaces of the aluminum parts as given in the flag notes of Figure 403. Refer to SRM 51-20-01 and SOPM 20-44-04. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-015 (3) Apply prepack sealant, A00247 as shown in Figure 403. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-016 (4) Apply fay surface seal to all part-to-part and part-to-shim interfaces with sealant, A00247 as shown in Figure 403 per SOPM 20-50-19. NOTE: Do not apply sealant to the electrical bonding path as shown in Figure 403. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-024 (5) Install the fasteners to secure the fairing [25] to the winglet as follows: (a) Tip fairing to leading edge skin: 1) Install two bolts [26] wet with sealant, A00247 per SOPM 20-50-19. 2) Install bolts [26] flush to flushness tolerance of -0.007 in. (-0.018 cm) to 0.000 in. (0.000 cm). (b) Tip fairing to skin panels: 1) Apply one coat primer, C00175 on all hole surfaces. Refer to SOPM 20-44-04. 2) Install rivets [27] as given in SRM 51-40-02. 3) Install rivets [27] wet with sealant, A00247 per SOPM 20-50-19, Method 2.. 4) Install rivets [27] flush to a flushness tolerance of -0.008 in. (-0.020 cm) to 0.000 in. (0.000 cm). NOTE: Shaving of spindle and head is permitted. (c) Tip fairing to the trailing edge arrowhead: 1) Install filler [28] between the tip fairing and arrowhead. a) If mismatch is not within tolerance, make a new filler from filler, G51401. Refer to Figure 403. b) Adjust the mismatch by selection of the correct thickness or by machining or sanding. Refer to SOPM 20-50-20. c) Install shim [29] between tip fairing and arrowhead as necessary. Refer to SOPM 20-50-20. d) Install rivets [27] double-flush and microshave rivets to a flushness tolerance of 0.003 in. (0.008 cm) to 0.000 in. (0.000 cm). SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-017 (6) Apply aerodynamic sealant to all peripheral external tip fairing gaps with sealant, A00247 as given in SOPM 20-50-11. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-018 (7) Fay surface electrical bond tip fairing to the leading edge skin and trailing edge arrowhead in the hatched areas shown in Figure 403. Refer to SOPM 20-11-03, Category One.

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 527 Left Winglet 627 Right Winglet

D. Winglet Bulb Seal Permitted Damage Limits

SUBTASK 57-21-21-210-003 (1) Permitted damage limits to the bulb seal at the wing to the winglet connection are as follows: (a) Cuts or tears fully through the silicone rubber membrane of the bulb seal are permitted, if the length of the cut or tear is 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) maximum. Multiple cuts or tears on a single seal are permitted only if the distance between the damage locations is 2.0 in. minimum. (b) Nicks or scratches in the silicone material that do not fully into the silicone rubber membrane of the bulb seal are permitted. (c) Cuts, tears, wearing, and fraying of the Dacron fabric material exposing the silicone rubber material are permitted. (d) Permanent setting/deformation of the bulb portion of the seal because of compression is permitted, if the protrusion dimension from the root of the winglet to the maximum protruding point of the seal is 0.140 in. (3.56 mm) minimum.

E. Winglet Bulb Seal Installation

SUBTASK 57-21-21-210-004 (1) Make sure that the winglet bulb seals are in the permitted damage limits. SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-039 (2) Install the forward seal [58] as follows: (a) Align the forward seal [58] and retainer with the attachment holes. (b) Install the forward seal [58] with the 11 bolts [43], 11 washers [44], and 11 nuts [45]. (c) Torque the bolts [43] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-040 (3) Install the forward upper seal [59] as follows: (a) Align the forward upper seal [59] and retainer with the attachment holes. (b) Install the forward upper seal [59] with the eight bolts [46], eight washers [47] and eight nuts [48]. (c) Torque the bolts [46] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-041 (4) Install the aft upper seal [61] as follows: 57-21-21 (a) Align the aft upper seal [61] and retainer with the attachment holes. (b) Install the aft upper seal [61] with the 13 bolts [49], 13 washers [50] and 13 nuts [51]. (c) Torque the bolts [49] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-042 (5) Install the forward lower seal [60] as follows: (a) Align the forward lower seal [60] and retainer with the attachment holes. (b) Install the forward lower seal [60] with the 10 bolts [52], nine washers [53] and nine nuts [54]. (c) Torque the bolts [52] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 57-21-21-420-043 (6) Install the aft lower seal [62] as follows: (a) Align the aft lower seal [62] and retainer with the attachment holes. (b) Install the aft lower seal [62] with the 12 bolts [55], 12 washers [56] and 12 nuts [57]. (c) Torque the bolts [55] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 57-21-21-410-005 (1) Do this task: Winglet Installation, TASK 57-21-21-400-801.

57-21-21-300-801Winglet - PaintingPDF p. 693

2. Winglet - Painting (Figure 701)

A. References

Reference Title 51-21-11 PAINT STRIPPING

B. General

SUBTASK 57-21-21-370-003 (1) Significant weight addition to the winglet may cause a condition dangerous to flight safety. For this reason, painting over existing finishes is not permitted unless specifically approved by Aviation Partners . Application of a new finish equivalent to the initial finish is permissible only if the original finish is stripped using this procedure: PAINT STRIPPING, SUBJECT 51-21-11. NOTE: Most of the exterior of the winglet is of composite construction, which may only be stripped abrasively. (2) The total top coat dry film thickness shall not exceed an average of 4.8 mils (0.12 mm).

C. Masking Requirements

SUBTASK 57-21-21-950-001 (1) The three polished leading edge skins from the winglet root up to, but not including the wingtip fairing. This includes the navigation lens assembly mounted in the inboard leading edge skin. SUBTASK 57-21-21-950-003 (2) The Drawing Identified Ground Support Equipment (GSE) attach locations that are not in use with exposed threads. NOTE: If a fastener is an installed at the GSE location, then masking is not required. SUBTASK 57-21-21-950-004 (3) Inboard surfaces at winglet station zero. Overspray is allowed onto inboard upper and lower skin edges. Overspray is not allowed on bulb seal. Refer to Figure 701 for overspray allowance and masking requirements. SUBTASK 57-21-21-950-005 (4) The exposed portion of the aft position light glass lens. SUBTASK 57-21-21-950-006 (5) If installed, the exposed portion of the anti-collision light glass lens.

57-21-21-100-801Seal Repair Procedure Surface PreparationPDF p. 695

2. Seal Repair Procedure Surface Preparation

A. General

(1) Make all of the seal repairs with the seal in a position for easy access and when the load on the seal is as small as possible. For seals that are installed, it can be necessary to remove parts of the seal retainer to do work on the damaged area. (2) Replace the seal if the damage is extensive.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00068 Alcohol - Denatured, Ethyl (Ethanol) AMS 3002, MIL-E-51454 Type II B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 B00137 Abrasive - Garnet Coated Paper B00148 Solvent - Methyl Ethyl Ketone (MEK) ASTM D740 57-21-21 (Continued) Reference Description Specification G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-21-21-010-004 (1) Make sure that there is access to the seal. (a) If it is necessary, remove one or more sections of the seal retainer to get access to a damaged section of the seal. SUBTASK 57-21-21-100-003 (2) Clean the area of the seals with the seal in a position for easy access, do the steps that follow: (a) Rub the area and approximately 2 in. (51 mm) or more on all sides of the area with a clean cotton wiper, G00034 that is wet with one of the solvents that follow: 1) solvent, B00148 2) alcohol, B00068 3) alcohol, B00130. (b) Lightly rub the surface to be repaired with the abrasive, B00137 (180 grit minimum). (c) Wipe dry with a cotton wiper, G00034 before solvent evaporates. 1) If necessary repeat steps to fully remove dirt, oil, paint, and other soils. NOTE: Clean surfaces are necessary to make a good bond.

57-21-21-350-801Seal Repair Procedures For Specified Types of Seal DamagePDF p. 696

3. Seal Repair Procedures For Specified Types of Seal Damage (Figure 801)

A. General

(1) Make all of the seal repairs with the seal in a position for easy access and when the load on the seal is as small as possible. For seals that are installed, it can be necessary to remove parts of the seal retainer to do work on the damaged area. (2) Determine the type of repair that is necessary and the procedure to be used. (a) Use fabric when a stronger bond is necessary. (b) Replace the seal if the damage is extensive. (c) Replace the repaired seal as quickly as possible. D. Repair Procedures for Specified Types of Seal Damage

SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-013 (1) Repair the damaged seal as follows (temporary repair): (a) Hold the surfaces together. (b) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the damaged area. (c) This repair is permitted until 90 days. 1) After 90 days, continue with the applicable repair procedure. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-010 (2) Repair a cut or split in the bulb section of a seal as follows: (a) If the damage is a small cut or split (0.20 in. (5.08 mm) maximum length), do these steps: 1) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method A), TASK 57-21-21-350-802 to bond the damaged seal with one of the adhesives in the tables that follow: a) Table Of Type I Adhesives/Table 801 b) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 c) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. 2) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. 3) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. 4) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area. (b) If the damage is a large cut or split (1.00 in. (25.40 mm) maximum length), do these steps: 1) Push on the seal to open the cut. 57-21-21 2) Carefully drill a hole in each end of the cut. NOTE: A sharpened metal tube can be used as a drill bit to cut the holes. 3) Make the holes smooth and miter the edges. 4) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method A), TASK 57-21-21-350-802 to bond the damaged seal with one of the adhesives in the tables that follow: a) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 b) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. 5) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. 6) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. 7) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area. (c) If the damage to the seal is a large split (2.00 in. (50.80 mm) maximum length), do these steps: 1) Push on the seal to open the cut. 2) Carefully drill a hole in each end of the cut. NOTE: A sharpened metal tube can be used as a drill bit to cut the holes. 3) Make the holes smooth and miter the edges. 4) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method B), TASK 57-21-21-350-803 to bond the damaged seal with one of the adhesives in the tables that follow: a) Table Of Type I Adhesives/Table 801 b) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 c) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. 5) Cut the fabric to make an overlap of 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) on the sides and ends of the split. 6) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. 7) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. 8) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-011 (3) Repair a damaged seal flange (3.00 in. (76.20 mm) maximum patch length) as follows: (a) If it is not necessary to replace the flange, do these steps: 1) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method B), TASK 57-21-21-350-803 to bond the damaged seal with one of the adhesives in the tables that follow: a) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 b) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. 2) Cut the fabric to make an overlap of 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) on the sides and ends of the split. 3) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. 4) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. 5) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area. 57-21-21 (b) If a part of the flange is missing, do these steps: 1) Trim the seal edge adjacent to the missing part of the flange. 2) Cut a piece of replacement flange that is a correct fit for the missing part. 3) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method C), TASK 57-21-21-350-804 to bond the replacement seal patch to the seal with one of the adhesives in the tables that follow: a) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 b) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. 4) Cut the fabric to make an overlap of 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) on the sides and ends of the split. 5) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. 6) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. 7) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area. SUBTASK 57-21-21-390-012 (4) Repair large damage to seal parts as follows: (a) Find the seal splices in the straight parts of the seal. (b) Remove the full damaged area. (c) Replace the damaged area with a piece of replacement seal that has the same dimensions. (d) Make mitered cuts on the seal surfaces that touch. (e) Fill them with adhesive from the tables that follow: 1) Table Of Type II Adhesives/Table 802 2) Table Of Type III Adhesives/Table 803. (f) Do the Seal Repair Procedure (Method B), TASK 57-21-21-350-803 and the Seal Repair Procedure (Method C), TASK 57-21-21-350-804 to bond the seal splices. (g) Push the surfaces tightly together to make sure that the adhesive fully touches the repair area. (h) Make sure that the adhesive cures the minimum time necessary. (i) Apply 3M 436 T ape, G50228 or the equivalent on the repaired area.

57-21-21-350-802Seal Repair Procedure (Method A)PDF p. 702

4. Seal Repair Procedure (Method A)

A. General

(1) This procedure is for repairs that uses only adhesive.

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-21-21-300-001 (1) Do the steps that follow to repair the seal with only adhesive: (a) Apply the adhesive to all of the areas to be bonded. (b) Put a load on the seal to make sure that the seal fully touches the adhesive. (c) Let the adhesive cure the minimum time necessary before you put a load on it.

57-21-21-350-803Seal Repair Procedure (Method B)PDF p. 702

5. Seal Repair Procedure (Method B)

A. General

(1) This procedure is for repairs with an adhesive reinforced with fabric. The fabric is embedded in the adhesive on the seal surface.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00028 Fabric - Dacron, (Mohawk Dacron Fabrics - D117 Fabric) G51094 Fabric - Dacron, 100/34 Solid (Mohawk Dacron Fabrics - D1000 Fabric)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-21-21-300-002 (1) Do the steps that follow to repair the seal with adhesive and fabric: (a) Cut the fabric to have the correct fit for the patch area. Use the fabrics that follow: 1) D1000 Dacron Fabric, G51094 for external covering. 2) D117 Dacron Fabric, G00028 for internal reinforcement (optional). (b) Apply the adhesive to the repair area on the seal. (c) Push the fabric patch into the wet adhesive and apply more adhesive on top of the patch. (d) Make the surface smooth of unwanted adhesive and put a load on to make sure that the seal fully touches the adhesive. (e) Apply pressure to make sure that the parts are fully bonded. (f) Let the adhesive cure the minimum time necessary before you put a load on it.

57-21-21-350-804Seal Repair Procedure (Method C)PDF p. 702

6. Seal Repair Procedure (Method C)

A. General

(1) This procedure replaces the damaged seal part with an equivalent piece of replacement seal. 57-21-21

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G00028 Fabric - Dacron, (Mohawk Dacron Fabrics - D117 Fabric) G51094 Fabric - Dacron, 100/34 Solid (Mohawk Dacron Fabrics - D1000 Fabric)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 57-21-21-300-003 (1) Do the steps that follow to repair the seal with an equivalent piece of replacement seal: (a) Cut a piece of replacement seal that will have the correct fit for the repair area. (b) Miter the seal and the replacement piece of seal to the correct fit. (c) Do one of the procedures that follow: 1) To repair the seal with only adhesive: a) Apply the adhesive to all of the areas to be bonded. b) Put a load on the seal to make sure that the seal fully touches the adhesive. c) Let the adhesive cure the minimum time necessary before you put a load on it. 2) To repair the seal with adhesive and fabric: a) Cut the fabric to have the correct fit for the patch area. Use one of the fabrics that follow: <1> D1000 Dacron Fabric, G51094 for external covering. <2> D117 Dacron Fabric, G00028 for internal reinforcement (optional). b) Apply the adhesive to the repair area on the seal. c) Push the fabric patch into the wet adhesive and apply more adhesive on top of the patch. d) Make the surface smooth of unwanted adhesive and put a load on to make sure that the seal fully touches the adhesive. e) Apply pressure to make sure that the parts are fully bonded. f) Let the adhesive cure the minimum time necessary before you put a load on it.

Lens Assembly Installation SUBTASK 57-21-22-420-005 (1) Attach the forward position light lens assembly [85] to the leading edge. (a) Attach the bonding jumper [87] to the lens assembly [85]. 1) Position the jumper lug and install the screw [83] and nut [84]. (b) Measure the electrical resistance between the lens assembly and light assembly (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use theintrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohm) or less. (c) Install the lens assembly [85]. NOTE: Fay seal is no longer used at this location. (d) Install the screws [81] with compound, C00528, and tighten to 10.00 in-lb (1.13 N·m) - 18.00 in-lb (2.03 N·m). (e) Apply an aerodynamic seal with sealant, A00160, sealant, A50231, or PR-1772 Class B Sealant, A50343, to the external gap around the lens (SOPM 20-50-19, SOPM 20-50-11). 1) If you must send the airplane before the sealant is fully cured, install 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, on the top of the sealant. a) Remove the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, when the sealant is fully cured (TASK 20-30-11-910-802). b) Carefully inspect the sealant and make sure that the sealant is adhered to the edges and that it is cured properly. SUBTASK 57-21-22-420-006 (2) Attach the anti-collision light lens assembly [88] to the leading edge. (a) Attach the bonding jumper [87] to the lens assembly [88]. 57-21-22 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH DUAL FORWARD LENS CONFIGURATION (Continued) 1) Position the jumper lug and install the screw [83] and nut [84]. (b) Measure the electrical resistance between the lens assembly and light assembly (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use the intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohm) or less. (c) Apply MS-122DF lubricant, D50119, or MS-122XD lubricant, D50326, to the faying surfaces of the anti-collision light lens assembly [88], except at electrical bonding locations. 1) Let the anti-collision light lens assembly [88] to dry. (d) Install the anti-collision light lens assembly [88]. (e) Install the screws [82] with compound, C00528, and tighten to 10.00 in-lb (1.13 N·m) - 18.00 in-lb (2.03 N·m). (f) Apply an aerodynamic seal with sealant, A00160, sealant, A50231, or PR-1772 Class B Sealant, A50343, to the external gap around the lens (SOPM 20-50-19, SOPM 20-50-11). 1) If you must send the airplane before the sealant is fully cured, install 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, on the top of the sealant. a) Remove the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, when the sealant is fully cured (TASK 20-30-11-910-802). b) Carefully inspect the sealant and make sure that the sealant is adhered to the edges and that it is cured properly. Forward Position Light and Anti-Collision Light Panel (Dual Forward Lens) Installation SUBTASK 57-21-22-420-007 (1) Install the forward position light and anti-collision light panel [91]. (a) Install the panel assembly for the forward position light and anti-collision light in the leading edge skin. (b) Apply primer, C00175, to the holes of the bolts [92], bolts [93], and bolts [94] (TASK 51-21-72-370-801). 1) Make sure that there is no primer in the countersinks. NOTE: A small quantity of unwanted primer in the countersinks is permitted for the bolts [92] and bolts [94]. (c) Apply compound, C00528, to all areas of the holes of the bolts [92], bolts [93], and bolts [94]. (d) Install the bolts [92], bolts [93], and bolts [94]. 1) Tighten the bolts [92], and bolts [93] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). 2) Tighten the bolts [94] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). SUBTASK 57-21-22-765-003 (2) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the leading edge skin and leading edge ribs (SWPM 20-20-00). (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (b) Make sure that the electrical resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 57-21-22-390-003 (3) Apply sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, at the gap between the leading edge panel [91] and outboard leading edge panel and the upper skin panel and lower skin panel. (a) Make the sealant smooth and flush with the adjacent surfaces with a hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810. 1) If it is necessary to send the airplane before the sealant is fully cured, do these steps: a) Allow sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, to cure as long as possible before applying 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. 57-21-22 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH DUAL FORWARD LENS CONFIGURATION (Continued) b) Install 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, on the sealant. c) Before each flight, visually examine the 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291. d) Remove 3M 425 Aluminum Foil T ape, G00291, when the sealant is fully cured (TASK 20-30-11-910-802). e) Carefully inspect sealant, A00247, or sealant, A50009, to make sure that the sealant is adhered to the edges and that it is has cured properly. f) If it is necessary, replace sealant.

Forward Position Light and Anti-Collision Light Lens (Dual Lens) Inspection SUBTASK 57-21-22-212-002 (1) Do a visual inspection of the exterior surface of the lens on the left and right winglet for these conditions: (a) Disbonding 1) No disbonding between the lens and lens retainer are allowed. (b) Cracks 1) The lens must not have any cracks. (c) Chipping 1) Use a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097, to measure and determine the length of chipping. 2) There must be no chipping in the lens area from 0 in. (0 cm) - 4 in. (10 cm) outboard of the inboard trim line. 3) The following is an allowable condition for a lens (Figure 601). a) Chipping is allowed in a limited area, 4 in. (10 cm) outboard of the inboard trim line. 57-21-22 b) For the area more than 4 in. (10 cm) outboard, the chip length cannot exceed 0.25 in. (0.64 cm) from the lens retainer inner trim line (measured normal to the trim line edge). (d) If the other lens has not been inspected, repeat this task for the other lens. (e) If both lenses have been inspected, this task is complete. SUBTASK 57-21-22-960-002 (2) If any of these conditions are seen, replace the lens. (a) Do this task: Forward Position Light and Anti-Collision Light Lens (Dual Forward Lens) Removal, TASK 57-21-22-000-803. (b) Do this task: Forward Position Light and Anti-Collision Light Lens (Dual Forward Lens) Installation, TASK 57-21-22-400-804.

57-21-22-910-801Polish the Leading Edge Light LensPDF p. 731

2. Polish the Leading Edge Light Lens (Figure 801)

A. General

(1) This task gives the instructions to polish the exterior surface of the lens on the left or right winglet.

B. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B50025 Compound - Polishing, Final Finish - NuShine IIS G50138 Cloth - Soft Cotton G50140 Gloves - Protective, Latex or Nitrile G50141 Towel - Paper, High Quality, Single Ply, White or Natural Colors

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 500 Left Wing 527 Left Winglet 600 Right Wing 627 Right Winglet

D. Leading Edge Light Lens Polish

SUBTASK 57-21-22-910-001 (1) Apply small amounts of NuShine IIS compound, B50025, along the leading edge of the lens. (a) Use a pair of protective gloves, G50140. (b) Do only half of the length of the lens at a time, or the polish will become dry too soon. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY PRESSURE TO THE SURFACE OF THE LENS. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE LENS. (c) Polish with high quality paper towel, G50141, with light pressure only in a linear motion along the leading edge. NOTE: Use only plain white or natural color paper towels. NOTE: There will be a transition line, approximately 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) wide between the hazed surface and the undamaged clear surface. Do not try to polish this portion of the lens, a hard coat material remains on the lens and can not be polish out to a clear state. SUBTASK 57-21-22-910-002 (2) Repeat the polish. 57-21-22 (a) After the polish is completed, use clean soft cotton cloth, G50138, in order to achieve a final luster.

57-21-23-790-801Vapor Seal Leak CheckPDF p. 753

2. Vapor Seal Leak Check (Figure 601)

A. General

006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-096 (1) Regulatory requirements refer to the Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) ST00830SE. NOTE: Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) ST00830SE changes some wing structures for retrofit installation of the Aviation Partners (APB) Blended Winglets. ALL (2) This task gives the procedure to do a check of the vapor seal of the inboard dry bay tank between rib 25 and rib 26. (3) The check requires pressurization of the dry bay tank for 10 minutes with a minimum pressure loss. (4) It is difficult to find the vapor leaks on the outside surface of the wing; the tank can be pressurized and a bubble solution applied to the wing. The bubbles will show the external leak points. (5) The pressure test equipment must be able to supply positive pressure, 2.5 ±0.6 psig (17.2 ±4.2 kPa). The maximum pressure to the structure is 3.0 psig (20.7 kPa) positive pressure and 2.0 psig (13.8 kPa) vacuum. A safety device which limits internal pressure to 72 in/H 2O (2.6 psig) and -20 in/H 2O (-0.7 psig) is required. (a) The water manometer, SPL-1774, does not have a mark for 72 in/H 2O (2.6 psig). It is recommended to put a temporary mark at the height of 31.25 in. (79.38 cm) measured from the top of the cross tube. Then the manometer tube could be filled to that height to provide a 2.6 psig (72.0 in/H 2O) safety relief manometer setting. (6) All plugs are installed from inside the dry bay tank (the pressure side) to prevent blowout of the plug. (7) The leading edge slats must be fully extended to install the block off plug in the forward spar. 57-21-23 (8) To prevent damage to the wing, all repairs to the wing structure must be completed before the tank is pressurized. (9) Only pressurize one tank at a time. No two adjacent tanks can be pressurized at the same time when you do a check for leakage from one tank to the adjacent tank. (10) All areas where the sealant was changed by damage or rework must be tested again to make sure that the seal is good. (11) All leak repairs must be tested again with this procedure.

H. Pressure Check Procedure

SUBTASK 57-21-23-790-001 (1) Do the pressure check. 57-21-23 (a) This task is extremely sensitive to the surrounding temperature changes. Avoid any unnecessary activities that might cause a change in temperature. (b) Supply 2.2 psig (15.2 kPa) - 2.4 psig (16.5 kPa) of air pressure to the test equipment. (c) Open the shut off valve on the pressure test door; the dry bay tank is now pressurized. (d) Wait 2 minutes minimum for the pressure in the tank to become stable before you start the check. (e) Close the shut off valve on the pressure test door. (f) Record the start time of the check and the inches of water at the beginning of the check. (g) Wait 10 minutes; the tank must hold the pressure for this time. (h) After 10 minutes, make a record of the inches of water on the manometer. (i) Calculate the pressure drop. 1) Subtract the value for the inches of water at the start of the check from the inches of water at the end of the check. 2) If the pressure drop is less than 0.11 in/H 2O (0.004 psig) or 0.11 in/H 2O (0.03 kPa), the vapor seal is good. a) Decrease the pressure in the tank to zero. b) Put the airplane back to the usual condition. 3) If the pressure drop is more than 0.11 in/H 2O (0.004 psig) or 0.11 in/H 2O (0.03 kPa), there is vapor movement through the vapor seal. a) Examine the pressure test door for leakage. <1> Apply a non-corrosive soap solution, leak detector, G50135, or Snoop Leak Detector compound, G00091, to the pressure test door. <2> If you find leakage, decrease the pressure in the tank to zero. <a> Repair the leak. <b> Do the Pressure Check Procedure again. <3> If you find no leakage, continue to the next step. b) Decrease the pressure in the tank to zero. c) Continue with the procedure to find the location of the vapor leak.
